text: ブラスカがシンと戦い、命を落とした後でな。
translation: That was after Braska fought Sin and lost his life.

vocabulary.meaning: to lose one's life, to die

grammar: 〜た後で expresses 'after doing (something).' The sentence ends with the sentence-final particle な (男性語), which adds a reflective or explanatory tone, common in Auron's speech.

text: 納得できなかったんだよ。 / あいつらの仇を討つために。
translation: I just couldn't accept it. / It was to avenge them.

vocabulary.meaning: to take revenge, to avenge someone
in order to, for the purpose of

grammar: 納得できなかったんだよ — the んだ adds an explanatory nuance ('the thing is, I couldn't accept it'). ために expresses purpose: 'in order to avenge them.'

text: もう一度ここに来て、帰り討ちだ
translation: I came back here once more — to strike back.

vocabulary.meaning: striking back; being killed by a retaliating enemy (lit. 'return attack')

grammar: 帰り討ち literally means being struck down when returning to fight — used here to mean 'going back to fight.' The sentence ends declaratively with だ, giving it a blunt, determined tone.

text: なんとか一命を取り留めて、ガガゼ島を這い降りたが
translation: I barely managed to survive and crawled down Mt. Gagazet, but…

vocabulary.reading: いちめいをとりとめる
vocabulary.meaning: to narrowly survive, to escape death

grammar: 〜て connects sequential actions: survived → crawled down. The sentence-final が leaves things hanging, implying 'but [something happened].'

text: ベベルの手前で力尽きてな
translation: My strength gave out just before reaching Bevelle.

vocabulary.meaning: just before, this side of (a location)
to run out of strength, to be exhausted

grammar: 力尽きて + な: the て-form links to the following clause; the sentence-final な adds a retrospective, slightly rueful tone — Auron reflecting on his own death.

text: その時会ったのが、キマリだ / ユーナを任せて、俺は死んだ
translation: That's when I met Kimahri. / I entrusted Yuna to him, and then I died.

vocabulary.meaning: to entrust, to leave (something) to someone

grammar: 〜のが is a nominalizer turning a verb phrase into a noun: 'the one I met was Kimahri.' The sentences are clipped and declarative — Auron's characteristic sparse, blunt delivery.

text: それ以来、異界にも行かず、こうしてさまよっている
translation: Ever since then, I haven't gone to the Farplane either — I've been wandering like this.

vocabulary.meaning: the Farplane, the realm of the dead

grammar: 〜ず is an archaic/literary negative form equivalent to 〜ないで ('without doing'). こうして means 'in this way.' The progressive 〜ている frames his wandering as an ongoing state.

text: アーロン / そんな顔をするな / こういう体で得したこともある
translation: Auron. / Don't make that face. / There are some perks to having a body like this.

vocabulary.meaning: to benefit, to gain an advantage

grammar: 〜するな is a negative imperative: 'don't do X.' こういう体 refers to being an unsent spirit. 〜こともある means 'there are times when / there are cases where.'

text: シンに乗って / お前のザナルカンドにも行け出しな
translation: I rode Sin — and even made it to your Zanarkand.

vocabulary.meaning: managed to get there, succeeded in going (informal/dialectal)

grammar: 乗って is the て-form connecting actions. 行け出し is a rough/informal expression implying 'managed to go.' The な at the end softens/emphasizes the statement in casual speech.

text: そんで / ずっと俺のこと
translation: And then… / you were watching over me all along…

vocabulary.meaning: and then, so (casual contraction of それで)
all along, the whole time, continuously

grammar: The sentence is left incomplete — Tidus trails off, overwhelmed. ずっと俺のことwould complete as 'watching over me the whole time,' with 見守って implied from the next line.

text: 見守ってくれたのか / どうして
translation: …you were watching over me? / Why…?

vocabulary.meaning: to watch over, to keep an eye on (protectively)
to do (something) for me/us (indicates a favor received)

grammar: 見守ってくれたのか — のか turns the sentence into a wondering/confirming question. The isolated どうして (without a full sentence) conveys Tidus's emotional disbelief.

text: どうしてそこまでするんだよあんた
translation: Why would you go that far for me, old man?

vocabulary.meaning: to that extent, that far, so much

grammar: するんだよ — the んだ adds emotional emphasis and demand for explanation. あんた placed at the end is conversationally emphatic, almost confrontational but also expressing raw vulnerability.

text: こういうことはな / 口では説明できるのだ
translation: Things like this… / can't really be explained in words.

vocabulary.meaning: things like this, this sort of matter

grammar: This line appears to contain a game transcription error (口では説明できるのだ likely should be 口では説明できないのだ — 'cannot be explained in words'). The negative meaning is implied by context: Jecht says he can't explain it, then shows instead.

text: いいだろ / 見せてやろう
translation: Fine then. / Let me show you.

vocabulary.meaning: to do (something) for someone (often with a rough or generous nuance)

grammar: 見せてやろう — やろう (volitional of やる) expresses a rough/generous intention: 'I'll show you.' This is Jecht's characteristically gruff way of expressing care.

text: 俺の記憶だ
translation: These are my memories.
grammar: A simple declarative sentence with だ. Short and weighty — Jecht reveals a vision of his past to Tidus.

text: 最後に一個だけいいか? / あのよ、わり、やっぱやめとくわ
translation: Can I ask just one last thing? / Actually… sorry, never mind, I'll skip it.

vocabulary.meaning: after all, as I thought (casual form of やはり)
to leave it, to not do after all (やめておく contracted)

grammar: いいか is a casual permission request: 'is it okay if…?' わり is short for 悪い ('bad/sorry'). やめとくわ — the わ at the end is a soft sentence-final particle expressing decision/resignation.

text: いいから言えよ
translation: Just say it already.

vocabulary.meaning: never mind that, just do it (dismissing hesitation)

grammar: 言えよ is an imperative (言え) + the emphatic particle よ: a direct command to speak. いいから dismisses the other person's hesitation: 'it doesn't matter, just say it.'

text: そうか、じゃあ行っちまうぞ / 息子を頼む
translation: I see. Well then, I'm going. / I'm counting on you for my son.

vocabulary.meaning: to go (and be gone); casual/rough for 行ってしまう
to ask, to request; I'm counting on you

grammar: 行っちまうぞ — ちまう is a casual/rough contraction of てしまう (indicating completion/finality); ぞ is an emphatic masculine particle. 頼む alone as a sentence is an urgent request: 'I'm counting on you.'

text: ザナルカンドもあいつを頼む
translation: And Zanarkand — count on him for that too.
grammar: The も adds 'Zanarkand too' to the previous request. Jecht is asking Auron to find a way to get Tidus to Zanarkand — the place Tidus came from.

text: あいつ泣き虫だからな
translation: That kid's a crybaby, you know.
grammar: だからな — the sentence-final な softens the statement into a rueful explanation. Jecht is talking about young Tidus affectionately despite using 泣き虫.

text: 誰かついててやんねえと心配で心配でよ
translation: If no one's there with him, I just can't stop worrying.

vocabulary.meaning: won't do (for someone); rough negative of やる

grammar: ついててやんねえと — conditional と: 'if someone doesn't stay with him.' 心配で心配で is a repetition for emphasis: 'so worried, so worried.' The よ at the end is an emphatic particle expressing Jecht's genuine anxiety.

text: だからよ
translation: That's why, you see.
grammar: だからよ — a fragment completing the thought: 'that's why [I'm asking you].' The よ adds a rough, personal emphasis common in Jecht's speech.

text: 頼むわ / しかしザナルカンドなんてどうやっていけば
translation: Please. / But how on earth would I even get to Zanarkand?

vocabulary.meaning: something like, a place like (adds a nuance of disbelief or distance)

grammar: 頼むわ — わ is a sentence-final particle here used by a male speaker for emphasis/resignation (different from female わ). しかし〜なんてどうやっていけば — the sentence is left incomplete (いけば without a result clause), conveying bewilderment.

text: なんで情けねえな / おめえの言う無限の可能性ってやつで
translation: Man, you're pathetic. / Use that 'infinite possibilities' thing you always talk about.

vocabulary.meaning: you (rough dialectal form of お前)

grammar: 情けねえ is a rough phonetic variant of 情けない. ってやつで — って quotes the phrase; やつ is a casual nominalizer ('that thing called…'); で indicates the means.

text: なんとかしてみろよ
translation: Give it a shot — figure something out.

vocabulary.meaning: to manage, to work something out

grammar: してみろ is the imperative of してみる — 'try doing it.' よ adds a rough encouragement. Together: 'go ahead and try to work it out.'

text: やってやろうじゃないか / 約束しよう
translation: I'll do it then! / Let's make a promise.

vocabulary.meaning: to do (something), often with a defiant or determined nuance
right?, let's (used to invite agreement or emphasize resolve)

grammar: やってやろうじゃないか — volitional of やってやる + じゃないか: a declaration of determined intent, roughly 'I'll damn well do it!' 約束しよう is the volitional form expressing a proposal: 'let's promise.'

text: あんたの息子は俺が守る
translation: I will protect your son.
grammar: 俺が is the subject marked with が for emphasis — 'I (specifically) will protect.' A direct, solemn promise from Auron.

text: 死んでも守ってやる / すまねえなアロン
translation: Even if I die, I'll protect him. / Sorry about this, Auron.

vocabulary.meaning: to protect (for someone's benefit, rough/generous nuance)
sorry, I'm sorry (rough form of 済まない)

grammar: 死んでも — 〜ても conditional: 'even if (I) die.' 守ってやる uses 〜てやる to indicate doing something for someone's benefit, with a rough masculine tone. すまねえ is Jecht's gruff way of saying 'sorry.'

text: おめえは片仏野郎だが / そういうとこ嫌いじゃなかったぜ
translation: You're a stiff, stubborn fellow — / but I didn't hate that about you.

vocabulary.meaning: a rigid, inflexible person; a stick-in-the-mud (lit. 'half-Buddha guy')
that kind of aspect/trait (contraction of そういうところ)
don't dislike, don't hate (double negative expressing mild affection)

grammar: 嫌いじゃなかったぜ — double negative (嫌いではない) in past tense with ぜ (emphatic masculine particle): 'wasn't something I disliked.' This is Jecht's closest thing to a compliment.

text: こういうことだ
translation: That's what it is.

vocabulary.meaning: this kind of thing, that's how it is

grammar: A closing declarative — Auron or Jecht summing up the explanation: 'this is what it comes down to.' Short and conclusive.

text: マジ?
translation: Seriously?

vocabulary.meaning: seriously, really (casual; short for マジで)

grammar: A one-word question expressing disbelief. マジ (from 真面目) is very common in casual Japanese speech.

text: もう少し… 待っててくれよな
translation: Just a little longer… wait for me, okay?

vocabulary.meaning: a little more, a little longer
please do (for me); requesting a favor

grammar: 待っててくれよな — 待って+て (progressive/ongoing) + くれ (favor request) + よな (seeking gentle agreement/confirmation). A soft, emotional appeal.

text: 究極召喚はないんだ / でも何とかするから
translation: There's no Final Summoning. / But I'll figure something out.

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん
vocabulary.meaning: Final Summoning (the summoning that defeats Sin but kills the summoner)
to manage, to work something out

grammar: ないんだ — explanatory んだ: 'the thing is, there is no Final Summoning.' でも〜から — 'but because I'll figure something out' → implying 'so wait for me.'

text: へぇ、しけたつるどなぁ / こうよ、見るんかも! / どこ行く、どこ行くってしつこいよ!
translation: Hmm, what a gloomy expression… / Hey, are you watching?! / 'Where are we going, where are we going' — stop pestering me!
grammar: These are rapid overlapping lines among the party (likely Rikku/Wakka bickering). しつこいよ — よ adds emphasis to the complaint. って marks repeated speech: 'keeps saying where are we going.'

text: 少しは自分でも考えてよね!
translation: Think for yourself a little bit!
grammar: 〜よね at the end combines よ (emphasis) + ね (seeking agreement), creating a mildly exasperated tone. でも emphasizes 'even on your own.'

text: どうする? / 明暗を期待しよう
translation: What do we do? / Let's hope for the best.

vocabulary.meaning: what to do, what shall we do
light and dark; here loosely: best outcome

grammar: 明暗を期待しよう — 期待しよう is the volitional form ('let's hope/expect'). 明暗 literally means 'light and darkness' but idiomatically refers to varying fortunes — 'let's hope for a good outcome.'

text: 一緒に考えろよ / そうだな、シンはジェクトだ / お前とシンは確かに通じ合っている / それが突破口になるかもしれん
translation: Think together with us! / You're right — Sin is Jecht. / You and Sin definitely have a connection. / That might be our way in.

vocabulary.meaning: to be connected, to understand each other, to resonate
might be, may be (casual/archaic form of かもしれない)

grammar: 通じ合っている — the progressive ている marks an ongoing state of connection. かもしれん is an older/rougher form of かもしれない, typical of Auron.

text: んで、どうすんだよ?
translation: So then, what do we actually do?

vocabulary.meaning: so, and then (casual contraction of それで/なので)
what are we gonna do? (casual: どうするんだよ)

grammar: Casual/spoken contractions: どうすんだよ = どうするんだよ. んだ adds a 'so, what's the deal?' nuance; よ adds impatience.

text: それがわかれば苦労はせん
translation: If we knew that, we wouldn't be struggling.

vocabulary.meaning: wouldn't do; archaic/dialectal negative of する

grammar: 〜ばconditionalis + negative: 'if X were true, (we) wouldn't Y.' せん is an older/formal negative form of する, characteristic of Auron. A wry, deadpan line.

text: だよな
translation: Yeah, fair enough.
grammar: だよな combines だ (copula) + よ (assertion) + な (seeking agreement) — a casual way to say 'yeah, that's right, isn't it.'

text: 私…ダメだね / 何だよ、いきなり
translation: I'm… useless, aren't I. / What's this, all of a sudden?
grammar: ダメだね — ね seeks gentle agreement/sympathy: 'I'm no good, am I.' 何だよ、いきなり — だよ is casual; いきなり alone as a follow-up expresses Tidus's surprise at Yuna's sudden self-criticism.

text: どうやってシンを倒すかずっと考えてる / けど、エヴォンの教えにないことは私にはわからなくて
translation: I've been thinking all along about how to defeat Sin. / But things that aren't in Yevon's teachings — I just don't know them.

vocabulary.meaning: not knowing, because (I) don't understand (te-form, trailing off)

grammar: 〜かずっと考えてる — indirect question (〜か) embedded as the object of 考える. わからなくて is a trailing te-form, expressing cause or leaving the thought incomplete ('because I don't know, so…').

text: ごめん / ユウナ、謝るな
translation: I'm sorry. / Yuna, don't apologize.
grammar: 謝るな — negative imperative (verb stem + な): 'don't apologize.' Tidus is direct and warm in stopping Yuna from blaming herself.

text: 逃げているように聞こえ / ユウナには似合わない / うん ありがとう キマリ / あのさ キマリは何かいい考えない? / エボンの教えだ
translation: It sounds like you're running away. / That doesn't suit you, Yuna. / Yes, thank you, Kimahri. / Hey, Kimahri — do you have any good ideas? / Yevon's teachings.

vocabulary.meaning: to sound like, to be heard as
to suit, to fit, to be becoming

grammar: 〜ように聞こえ — ように indicates manner/resemblance: 'sounds like (running away).' The line is cut short (聞こえ without ending), blending into the next speaker. 似合わない is a simple negative: 'doesn't suit.'

text: 教えじゃシンは倒せないよ / 教えの中に答えはない
translation: The teachings can't defeat Sin. / The answer is not within the teachings.
grammar: 教えじゃ — じゃ is a casual contraction of では, meaning 'with/by the teachings.' 倒せない is the potential form + negative: 'cannot defeat.' A direct, logical statement from Kimahri.

text: 答えは教えの外にある / 教えの中と外を知れば答えは見つかる
translation: The answer lies outside the teachings. / If you know both inside and outside the teachings, you will find the answer.

vocabulary.meaning: to be found, to be discovered

grammar: 知れば〜見つかる — conditional: 'if you know X, then Y.' Kimahri's philosophical, spare style uses parallel structure (中と外) for contrast.

text: 教えか… / キマリならマイカに聞く
translation: The teachings, huh… / If it's Kimahri, I'd ask Maika.

vocabulary.meaning: if it's (the case of), speaking of

grammar: 教えか — the か adds a reflective, musing tone: 'the teachings, is it...' キマリなら — conditional なら: 'if it's Kimahri (asking)' or 'if it were me, Kimahri.' Kimahri proposes consulting Grand Maester Mika.

text: 力づくでも喋らせる / それだ! 決まりすげえよ!
translation: I'll make him talk even by force. / That's it! Settled — that's amazing!

vocabulary.meaning: to make (someone) talk (causative of 喋る)

grammar: 〜でも: 'even by X means.' 喋らせる is the causative form of 喋る. 決まり as an exclamation means 'it's decided!' すげえ is a rough form of すごい ('amazing, incredible').

text: おい! すんげえこと考えたぞ!
translation: Hey! I just thought of something incredible!

vocabulary.meaning: incredible, amazing (intensified rough form of すごい)
to think, to come up with

grammar: 考えたぞ — past tense + ぞ (strong emphatic masculine particle): 'I thought of it!' すんげえ is a highly colloquial intensification of すごい.

text: あたしが思いついたんだよ! あたしに言わせなよ!
translation: I'm the one who thought of it! Let me say it!

vocabulary.meaning: to think of, to come up with an idea
to let (someone) say, to allow to speak (causative)

grammar: あたしが — が marks emphatic subject: 'I (specifically) thought of it.' 言わせなよ — causative (言わせる) + な (soft imperative) + よ: 'let me say it!' Rikku is eagerly claiming credit.

text: 要するにだな / えーっとね
translation: In short — / Um, let me see…

vocabulary.meaning: in short, to put it simply
um, let me see (filler while thinking)

grammar: 要するにだな — Wakka starting to explain; だな is a rough confirmation marker. えーっとね — Rikku jumping in with a filler, ne softens her taking over the explanation.

text: 歌が鍵よ
translation: Song is the key.
grammar: A simple declarative sentence. The sentence-final よ (feminine/emphatic) gives it a bright, confident energy — Rikku delivering the big idea.

text: 歌って? / ジェクトさんは祈りの歌が好き / そうでしょ
translation: Song? / Mr. Jecht loves the Hymn of the Fayth, / right?
grammar: 歌って? — って used as a quotation/topic marker + rising intonation = 'You mean song?' そうでしょ is a confirmation request, the short form of そうでしょう (isn't that right?).

text: だからマカラーニョコの底で歌を聞いてたんだよね
translation: That's why Sin was listening to the song at the bottom of Macalania.
grammar: 〜てたんだよね — ていた (progressive/past) contracted to てた + んだ (explanatory) + よね (seeking confirmation). 'That's why Sin was listening there, right?'

text: あれほど凶暴なシンが静かに歌を聞いていた
translation: Sin — as ferocious as it is — was quietly listening to the song.

vocabulary.meaning: to that degree, as (ferocious) as that

grammar: あれほど〜な — 'as X as that'; modifying 凶暴. 聞いていた is past progressive: 'was listening.' The contrast (ferocious yet quiet) is the rhetorical point.

text: あのな、お前の親父さんのことだから言いにくいけどよ / うん、いいって
translation: Look, it's about your dad, so it's hard to say this, but… / Yeah, go ahead, it's fine.

vocabulary.meaning: hard to say, difficult to bring up
it's fine, don't worry about it (casual dismissal)

grammar: 〜だから〜けどよ — causal だから + concessive けど + emphatic よ: 'because of X, it's hard to say, but…' いいって — って is a casual quotation/dismissal marker meaning 'I'm saying it's fine.'

text: どうしようもないんだからさ
translation: There's nothing we can do about it, after all.

vocabulary.meaning: there's nothing that can be done, hopeless, inevitable

grammar: 〜んだから — explanatory んだ + causal から: 'the thing is, because there's nothing we can do.' さ at the end is a soft emphatic particle adding a resigned/matter-of-fact tone.

text: じゃあ、言うわね
translation: Alright then, I'll say it.
grammar: 言うわね — わ is a feminine sentence-final particle adding a soft assertive tone; ね seeks mild agreement/acknowledgment. Lulu or Rikku steeling herself to speak plainly.

text: 正面からシンに立ち向かっても到底勝ち目はないわ / けれど、祈りの歌を聞かせればシンはおとなしくなる
translation: Even if we face Sin head-on, we stand no chance at all. / But if we let Sin hear the Hymn of the Fayth, Sin will become docile.

vocabulary.meaning: no matter what, not by any means (used with negatives)
chance of winning, prospect of victory
to let hear, to play (a song) for someone (causative of 聞く)

grammar: 〜ても到底〜はない: even if + absolutely no X. 聞かせれば — conditional of causative: 'if (we) let (Sin) hear.' おとなしくなる — 〜くなる means 'to become (adjective).'

text: その隙をつけば、なんとかなるんじゃねえか? / まあ、反則かもしれねえけどよ、こだわってらんねえしな
translation: If we exploit that opening, maybe we can pull through, right? / Well, it might be bending the rules, but we can't afford to be picky.

vocabulary.meaning: to exploit an opening, to take advantage of a gap
to work out somehow, to manage
to be particular about, to be hung up on

grammar: その隙をつけば — conditional ば: 'if we exploit that gap.' こだわってらんねえ — contracted from こだわっていられない: 'can't afford to care about that.' し+な adds a casual rationale.

text: ね、すごい作戦でしょ? / ああ、試す勝ち、ありだな
translation: Right? It's a great plan, isn't it? / Yeah, it's worth a shot — I'd say so.

vocabulary.meaning: that works, that's an option (ある + だな)

grammar: でしょ is the casual form of でしょう (seeking confirmation). 試す勝ちあり — a compact expression: '(it has) worth trying.' ありだな — colloquial: 'yeah, that's a valid option.'

text: 今さら、何をしろというのだ
translation: At this point, what are you telling me to do?

vocabulary.meaning: at this late stage, now of all times
what do you mean by saying/telling to do X (formal/indignant)

grammar: 何をしろというのだ — 何をしろ is a command ('do what'), embedded with というのだ expressing indignation or incredulity: 'what is it you're telling me to do?' Grand Maester Mika speaking in formal register.

text: 早くシンを倒せばよかろう
translation: You should just hurry up and defeat Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: it would be fine, one should (archaic volitional of いい)

grammar: 〜ばよかろう — conditional ば + archaic よかろう (= よいだろう): 'it would be fine if you do X' → effectively 'you should just.' Mika speaks in a stilted, archaic register.

text: 究極召喚を得たのであろう
translation: You must have obtained the Final Summoning.
grammar: 〜のであろう is an archaic/formal presumptive expression, equivalent to 〜はずだろう: 'it must be the case that.' Mika assumes the party followed the orthodox path.

text: 言うなれずかにあったけどさ
translation: Well, there was something I hesitated to say…

vocabulary.meaning: to become accustomed (here colloquially softening hesitation)
there was, existed (past tense of ある)
but, though (casual sentence-ending, inviting listener's attention)

grammar: This is a colloquially delivered line, slightly garbled in transcription — likely 「言いにくいことがあったけどさ」 (there was something hard to say, but…). けどさ trails off, leaving the thought open and inviting a response.

text: 私たちで倒しました / なんと
translation: We defeated it ourselves. / What!?

vocabulary.meaning: by means of, with (particle indicating means/agent)

grammar: 私たちで uses the particle で to indicate the agent group — 'by us ourselves.' The polite ました form shows Yuna speaking formally to Grand Maester Mika. なんと is an exclamation expressing astonishment.

text: もはや召喚師とガードが / 究極召喚の犠牲になることはない
translation: No longer will the summoner and guardians have to sacrifice themselves for the Final Summoning.

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん
vocabulary.meaning: Final Summoning (the ultimate summoning that defeats Sin)
there is no need to become ~, will not become ~

grammar: 〜になることはない expresses 'there is no longer a need to become X.' もはや (no longer) reinforces the finality. Yuna is declaring to Mika that the old cycle of sacrifice is over.

text: 一千年の断りを消し去ったというのか
translation: Are you saying you have erased a thousand years of tradition?

vocabulary.meaning: rule, principle, tradition (here: the established law/teaching)
to erase completely, to wipe out

grammar: 〜というのか is an accusatory rhetorical question pattern, expressing disbelief. Mika cannot fathom that the party has overturned a millennium of Yevon's doctrine.

text: この大たわけ者どもが
translation: You utter fools!
grammar: この大たわけ者どもが — the sentence is left grammatically incomplete (ends with が), which in Japanese conveys furious outrage, as though Mika is so livid he cannot finish his sentence. ども is a contemptuous plural.

text: 何をしたか / わかっておるのか
translation: Do you understand what you have done?

vocabulary.meaning: archaic/dialect form of ている (ongoing state)

grammar: わかっておるのか uses the archaic おる instead of いる, giving Mika's speech an old-fashioned, authoritative tone. のか at the end makes the question sharp and accusatory.

text: シンを鎮める / ただ一つの方法であったもの
translation: That was the one and only way to calm Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: to calm, to suppress, to pacify
thing; here used at sentence end to add emphasis/assertion

grammar: であったもの uses the literary past copula であった plus the nominalizer もの to add a weighty, assertive tone — 'that WAS the one and only way.' Mika is lamenting what he sees as the destruction of the only solution.

text: ただ一つなんて決めつけんなよ / 新しい方法考えてる
translation: Don't go claiming it's the only one! / We're thinking of a new way.

vocabulary.meaning: such a thing as ~, calling it ~ (dismissive particle)
to conclude arbitrarily, to insist dogmatically

grammar: 決めつけんなよ is a casual/rough prohibition: 決めつける + するな (don't) collapsed colloquially into 〜んな + よ for added assertion. Tidus pushes back against Mika's fatalism.

text: そのような方法など / ありはせぬわ
translation: No such method exists.

vocabulary.meaning: does not exist (emphatic archaic negative of ある)
sentence-final particle (here giving Mika's speech a sharp, dismissive tone)

grammar: ありはせぬ is an emphatic archaic negative — ある + は (contrastive/emphatic) + せぬ (archaic negative). The は inside adds strong emphasis: 'there is absolutely no such thing.' など dismisses the idea contemptuously.

text: 尻尾を巻いて異界に逃げるか / スピラの救いは失われた
translation: Are you going to tuck your tail and flee to the Farplane? / Spira's salvation is lost.

vocabulary.meaning: to tuck one's tail, to flee in shame (idiom)
the Farplane, the realm of the dead

grammar: 尻尾を巻いて逃げる is an idiom for running away shamefully. The か ending on the first clause is a rhetorical question — Tidus challenges Mika. The second clause is a bleak declaration by Mika.

text: もはや破滅は免れえぬ / エボンジュが作り上げた
translation: Destruction can no longer be avoided. / What Yunalesca created…

vocabulary.meaning: to escape, to be spared from
to build up, to construct, to create

grammar: 免れえぬ is archaic — 免れ (stem of 免れる) + え (potential auxiliary) + ぬ (archaic negative). Literally 'cannot escape.' This elevated register marks Mika as an old, formal authority figure.

text: 死の螺旋に落ちゆくのみよ / わしはスピラの終焉を見通ない
translation: All that remains is to fall into the spiral of death. / I will not witness the end of Spira.

vocabulary.meaning: spiral of death (a key phrase in FFX)
to fall gradually, to sink into (literary: 落ちていく)
to see through to the end, to witness completely

grammar: 落ちゆく is a literary contraction of 落ちていく (to continue falling). のみ (only) gives a fatalistic, formal tone. わし is the pronoun used by elderly male characters in Japanese. 見通ない appears to be a transcription of 見とうない (don't want to witness) — Mika's exit line.

text: 終わりにはしません / なあエボンジュって
translation: We won't let it end. / Hey, about Yunalesca…

vocabulary.meaning: will not let ~ happen (strong volitive negative)

grammar: 終わりにはしません — 〜にはしない is an emphatic refusal pattern: 'I will absolutely not make it X.' Yuna asserts her resolve. The second speaker then pivots the topic to Yu Yevon with なあ…って, a casual way to bring up a subject.

text: ユーナレスカ様もおっしゃってたわ
translation: Lady Yunalesca mentioned it too.

vocabulary.meaning: Lady Yunalesca (様 is an honorific suffix)
to say (honorific form of 言う)
was doing ~, had been saying ~ (casual contraction of ていた)

grammar: おっしゃってたわ — おっしゃる is an honorific verb for 'say.' Even though Yunalesca was an antagonist, the character uses 様 and honorific speech out of ingrained respect. わ at the end marks female speech.

text: ちょっとじいさん / エヴォンジュって何なのよ
translation: Hey, old man — what exactly is Yu Yevon?

vocabulary.meaning: hey, a moment (used as an attention-getter)
as for ~, speaking of ~ (casual topic marker)

grammar: Rikku's direct, casual speech: じいさん without a title is blunt. 何なのよ combines 何 + なの (explanatory) + よ (assertive, here making it an emphatic question). The よ gives a slightly impatient, demanding tone.

text: 死せる魂を寄せ集め / 鎧に変えて纏う者
translation: One who gathers the souls of the dead, transforms them into armor, and wears them.

vocabulary.meaning: the dead (literary/classical form of 死んでいる)
to wear, to drape oneself in

grammar: 死せる is a classical Japanese construction (死す + る attributive) meaning 'the dead.' This archaic phrasing suits the ancient, mythological nature of Yu Yevon. The sentence ends with 者, making the whole phrase a noun-modifying clause describing what Yu Yevon is.

text: その鎧こそ / シンに他ならぬ
translation: That armor is none other than Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: is nothing other than ~, is precisely ~ (formal expression)

grammar: こそ is an emphatic particle that highlights the subject — 'that armor, precisely.' 〜に他ならぬ is a formal expression meaning 'is nothing other than.' Together, these create a powerful declarative: Sin IS the armor Yu Yevon wears.

text: シンは / エヴォンジュを守る鎧
translation: Sin is the armor that protects Yu Yevon.
grammar: A simple but revelatory sentence. エヴォンジュを守る modifies 鎧 — 'the armor that protects Yu Yevon.' The copula だ is dropped, giving the statement a blunt, declarative weight. This is the key lore reveal of the scene.

text: その鎧を打ち破る究極召喚を
translation: The Final Summoning that could shatter that armor…

vocabulary.meaning: to smash through, to shatter, to break down

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん

grammar: This clause is left hanging — the sentence ends with を (object particle) without a verb, indicating the thought continues into the next segment. This creates dramatic suspense, building toward the accusation in clip_083.

text: お前たちが消し去った / 誰も倒せぬ
translation: …you lot have destroyed. Now no one can defeat it.
grammar: This completes the hanging sentence from clip_082. お前たちが消し去った is the predicate for 究極召喚を — 'the Final Summoning… you destroyed.' 倒せぬ is archaic negative potential (倒せない), reinforcing Mika's archaic speech register.

text: ふざけやがって! 好き勝手ほざいて逃げやがった!
translation: That bastard! He said whatever he pleased and just ran off!

vocabulary.meaning: to fool around, to mess around
contemptuous auxiliary verb (expressing anger at someone's action)
to blurt out, to say foolishly (vulgar/contemptuous)

grammar: 〜やがる is an extremely strong contemptuous suffix used when speaking angrily about someone's actions — it cannot be used respectfully. ほざく is a vulgar verb for speaking. Combined, these convey Tidus's furious reaction to Mika disappearing into the Farplane.

text: あの… マイカー総老子は? / あ…あの…
translation: Um… where is Grand Maester Mika? / Ah… um…

vocabulary.meaning: Grand Maester Mika (マイカー = Mika, 総老子 = Grand Maester)

grammar: The は after the subject leaves the sentence without a predicate — a very common Japanese pattern for asking 'where is X?' or 'what about X?' with the predicate implied. The あ…あの… from the other speaker shows flustered hesitation.

text: まだ来ないぞ いつまで待たせる気だ?
translation: He's still not here. How long do you intend to keep us waiting?

vocabulary.meaning: to make wait, to keep waiting (causative of 待つ)

grammar: 待たせる is the causative form of 待つ — 'to make someone wait.' 〜つもりだ / 〜気だ asks about someone's intention. いつまで待たせる気だ? is an idiomatic way to express impatient frustration: 'Just how long are you planning to keep us waiting?'

text: 変ですね… 私、探してきますね
translation: That's strange… I'll go look for him.

vocabulary.meaning: isn't it, that's ~ (polite sentence-ending seeking soft agreement)
to search for, to look for
to go and do ~, to do ~ and come back

grammar: 探してきます combines 探す + てくる — 'to go search and come back,' implying a short errand. The ね at the end softens the declaration. This is typical polite, deferential speech from a temple attendant.

text: お前… / 僕の部屋へ来て
translation: You… / Come to my room.

vocabulary.meaning: come (te-form of 来る used as a casual imperative)

grammar: 来て as a bare te-form functions as a soft command. The use of 僕 (Seymour's pronoun) alongside the address to Yuna signals Seymour pulling her aside privately. The unfinished お前… adds an eerie, possessive quality.

text: 誰と話してんだ? / ああ、なんでもないよ
translation: Who are you talking to? / Oh, it's nothing.

vocabulary.meaning: casual contraction of ているんだ (what are you doing?)

grammar: 話してんだ is a casual contraction: 話している + んだ → 話してんだ. The んだ demands an explanation. ああ、なんでもない is a deflective response — Yuna waves off the question, not wanting to reveal Seymour's ghost spoke to her.

text: 祈り子様に会いに行ってきます
translation: I'm going to go meet the fayth.

vocabulary.meaning: fayth (the beings whose souls power summoning)
to go to meet (〜に行く = go in order to ~)
to go and do ~ and come back (polite)

grammar: 会いに行ってきます — 行く (go) + てくる (come back after doing) combined with 会いに (in order to meet). This compound expresses going somewhere to do something and returning. 様 after 祈り子 shows Yuna's reverence for the fayth.

text: なるほどな
translation: I see.

vocabulary.meaning: I see, indeed, that makes sense

grammar: なるほど is an acknowledgment of understanding. The な at the end (masculine reflective particle) suggests Auron is speaking — he processes what Yuna said with quiet recognition. A brief but characteristically understated response.

text: やあ いつもお世話になっています
translation: Hey — thank you as always for everything.

vocabulary.word: お世話になっています
vocabulary.reading: おせわになっています
vocabulary.meaning: thank you for your help/care (set polite expression of gratitude)

grammar: お世話になっています is a fixed polite expression used to thank someone for ongoing assistance or care. It literally means 'I am being taken care of by you.' Tidus uses やあ as a casual greeting to the fayth, then shifts to formal gratitude — an endearing mix of registers.

text: で、なんだ?
translation: So, what is it?

vocabulary.meaning: so, then (conjunctive, moving to the point)

grammar: で as a sentence-opener here means 'so then' or 'well then' — a brisk pivot to business. なんだ? is a casual, slightly blunt question. The fayth speaks in a boyish, direct way, which characterizes his personality throughout FFX.

text: シンを復活させずに倒す方法、わかった?
translation: Have you figured out a way to defeat Sin without it coming back?

vocabulary.meaning: without letting ~ happen (causative + ずに = without doing)
understood, figured out (past of わかる)

grammar: させずに — causative (させ) + ずに (without doing): 'without causing Sin to revive.' The ずに form negates the action while linking it to the main clause. わかった? with rising intonation is a casual direct question.

text: うーんと…
translation: Hmm…
grammar: A filler expressing the fayth is thinking — characteristic of his childlike speech pattern. The trailing … conveys hesitation before the answer.

text: どうするの?
translation: What will you do?
grammar: どうするの? — the の softens the question, giving it a gentle, curious tone. The fayth asks what plan the party has in mind, inviting them to share their thinking.

text: 祈りの歌を聞かせれば、シンはおとなしくなる
translation: If we let him hear the Hymn of the Fayth, Sin will calm down.

vocabulary.meaning: Hymn of the Fayth (literal: prayer song)
to let hear, to play for (causative of 聞く)

grammar: 聞かせれば is the conditional (ば-form) of 聞かせる (causative). The structure is: 'if we make X hear the song, Y will happen.' おとなしくなる — おとなしい adjective becomes a verb via になる (to become quiet).

text: うーん、どうかな?
translation: Hmm, I wonder about that?

vocabulary.meaning: I wonder, will that work? (expressing doubt)

grammar: どうかな expresses gentle skepticism — 'I wonder if that will work.' な at the end is the reflective particle indicating the speaker is thinking aloud rather than flatly refusing. The fayth is uncertain but not dismissive.

text: ダメですか? / 君の父さんがシンになってから、もうずいぶん経ってるよ
translation: Will it not work? / It's already been quite a long time since your father became Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: after doing ~ (temporal: since the time of)

grammar: 〜てから emphasizes the starting point of an elapsed duration: 'since the time your father became Sin.' もうずいぶん経っている — もう (already) + ずいぶん (quite a lot) + 経っている (time has passed) — expresses that significant time has elapsed and things may have changed.

text: もう、歌は聞こえないかもしれない
translation: He may not be able to hear the song anymore.

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to hear, to be audible

grammar: 聞こえない is the negative of 聞こえる (the spontaneous/potential 'to be heard'). かもしれない expresses uncertainty. The fayth is saying Jecht's connection to music may have faded over the years trapped inside Sin — a quietly devastating line.

text: そうかもしれないけどさ / でも可能性があるなら賭けてみたいんだ
translation: That might be true, but… / Still, if there's a possibility, I want to bet on it.

vocabulary.meaning: but, though (casual, leaving space for continuation)
to bet, to wager, to stake on

grammar: 〜てみたい — te-form + みる (try doing) + たい (want to). The んだ at the end adds personal emotional weight, expressing Tidus's sincere desire rather than a casual statement. でも... starts a contrasting clause, showing stubborn optimism.

text: そうだね
translation: You're right.

vocabulary.meaning: yeah, you're right, that's true (agreeing warmly)

grammar: そうだね is a warm, casual agreement. The fayth uses ね rather than な, giving a gentle, slightly wistful tone — he's moved by Tidus's sincerity.

text: 君のそういうところ
translation: That part of you…
grammar: The sentence is incomplete — ending with ところ (aspect/place) without a predicate. This creates suspense, drawing the listener into the next segment where the thought is completed. そういうところ refers to Tidus's quality of refusing to give up.

text: 感心しちゃうな本当に / 俺はただの夢じゃない
translation: It really does impress me. / I'm not just a dream.

vocabulary.meaning: casual contraction of てしまう (can't help but, end up doing)

grammar: 感心しちゃうな — 〜てしまう (end up doing, can't help but) contracted to ちゃう. な is a reflective particle: 'I can't help but be impressed.' The second line 俺はただの夢じゃない is Tidus's sudden, quiet assertion — a foreshadowing of his nature as a dream of the fayth.

text: 夢?
translation: A dream?
grammar: A single-word question — the fayth picking up on Tidus's cryptic self-reference with curiosity. The rising intonation (implied by context) makes 夢 into a question. Short, reactive lines like this are common in natural Japanese conversation.

text: ああこっちの話 / それからどうするの?
translation: Ah, never mind that. / So then, what do you plan to do next?

vocabulary.meaning: talk on my side, something I was thinking (dismissive)

grammar: こっちの話 literally means 'a story on my end/side' — a casual way to wave off a remark as private thoughts. Tidus immediately redirects, both to avoid the topic and to refocus. それから moves the conversation forward.

text: 歌だけじゃ倒せないよ
translation: The song alone won't defeat it.

vocabulary.meaning: with just ~, by ~ alone (limitation particle + casual contraction of では)

grammar: だけじゃ is the casual contraction of だけでは — 'with only X.' The potential negative 倒せない explains a limitation. The fayth is steering them toward needing to confront Yu Yevon directly.

text: うーんと
translation: Hmm…
grammar: Another characteristic filler from the fayth, showing he is thinking before speaking. Repeated hesitation markers make his speech feel natural and childlike.

text: どうするの?
translation: So what will you do?
grammar: A repeat of the question from earlier, now echoed back — the fayth is prompting the party to articulate their plan. の softens the question.

text: エボンジュ、倒す / そう、エボンジュを倒せば、終わる
translation: Defeat Yu Yevon. / Right — if we defeat Yu Yevon, it will be over.

vocabulary.meaning: if we defeat ~ (conditional ば-form of potential 倒せる)

grammar: Tidus states the goal bluntly — subject dropped, just verb: 倒す. The fayth then restates it as a conditional: 〜を倒せば、終わる (if we defeat ~, it ends). The ば conditional is used here as a logical consequence chain.

text: ねえ、エボンジュのこと、どれぐらい知ってる? / シンが復活する鍵
translation: Hey, how much do you know about Yu Yevon? / He is the key to Sin's revival.
grammar: 〜のことを知ってる? — using のこと as a topic circumlocution: 'about Yu Yevon, how much do you know?' This is a natural Japanese pattern. The fayth's answer drops the copula: シンが復活する鍵 (is the key to Sin reviving) — a fragmentary, direct answer.

text: シンという鎧をまとった存在
translation: A being draped in the armor called Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: to wear, to be draped in

grammar: A relative clause modifying 存在 — 'a being who is draped in the armor called Sin.' シンという鎧をまとった is an attributive (modifying) clause in past tense. This rephrases the lore established by Mika in different words, confirming the party's understanding.

text: エボンジュはね、昔召喚師だった
translation: Yu Yevon, you see, was once a summoner.

vocabulary.meaning: you know, you see (soft sentence-internal particle inviting attention)
long ago, once upon a time

grammar: The ね inserted mid-sentence (エボンジュはね) is a characteristic feature of the fayth's speech — it invites the listener to pay attention and gives a storytelling quality. 昔〜だった sets the past context.

text: あれほどの召喚師はいない
translation: There is no summoner like him.

vocabulary.meaning: to that extent, that much (referring to the degree previously mentioned)
does not exist (は + いない, emphatic non-existence)

grammar: あれほど refers to a degree already understood from context ('to the extent he was'). はいない — は (contrastive/emphatic) + いない — stresses non-existence: there has NEVER been such a summoner. A strong superlative.

text: でも今はただ召喚を続けているだけの存在
translation: But now he is merely an existence that only continues to summon.
grammar: ただ〜だけ doubly emphasizes 'merely/only' — ただ (only) and だけ (only) together create a strong sense of limitation. 召喚を続けている is an ongoing progressive action. The contrast with the previous line (once the greatest summoner, now reduced to this) is poignant.

text: 悪意も善意もなく永遠の夢を願っているだけの存在
translation: A being with neither malice nor goodwill, only wishing for an eternal dream.
grammar: 悪意も善意もなく — AもBもなく: 'without either A or B.' This structure negates both alternatives. The sentence describes Yu Yevon as a tragic figure: not evil, not good, just endlessly wishing for something impossible. 永遠の夢 (eternal dream) echoes the game's central theme.

text: 永遠なんてないのにね
translation: Even though there's no such thing as eternity.

vocabulary.meaning: such a thing as ~, the very idea of ~ (dismissive/wistful)

grammar: のに expresses a resigned contrast — 'even though eternity doesn't exist.' It implies sadness about the impossibility. なんて dismisses 'eternity' as an illusion. The ね invites the listener's empathy. One of the most thematically rich lines in the scene.

text: 俺たちが終わらせるからな
translation: We'll put an end to it.

vocabulary.meaning: to bring to an end, to finish (causative of 終わる)
because, since (giving reason; な adds masculine assertion)

grammar: 終わらせる is the causative of 終わる — 'to cause it to end.' からな at the end gives a reason while asserting resolve: 'because we're going to end it.' The な (masculine) adds a sense of declaration and determination.

text: エボンジュは倒せない エボンジュは究極召喚獣に乗り移って
translation: Yu Yevon cannot be defeated. Yu Yevon takes over the aeon of the Final Summoning and…

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかんじゅう
vocabulary.meaning: the aeon of the Final Summoning
to take over, to possess, to transfer into

grammar: 倒せない is the potential negative: 'cannot defeat.' 乗り移って is the te-form, connecting to the next clause (the sentence continues in clip_120). 乗り移る means to transfer one's spirit into something — here Yu Yevon possesses the summoned aeon.

text: それを新しいシーンに作り変えてしまう エボンジュが
translation: …transforms it into a new Sin. Yu Yevon…

vocabulary.meaning: to end up doing ~, to do completely (often with undesirable result)

grammar: 作り変えてしまう — 〜てしまう adds a sense of completion and often regret: 'ends up transforming it entirely.' The sentence is split across clips, with エボンジュが left hanging at the end to continue into the next segment.

text: 乗り移る そして新しいシーンに守られて
translation: …takes over. And protected by the new Sin…

vocabulary.meaning: to be protected (passive of 守る)

grammar: 守られて is the passive te-form: 'being protected by ~.' The te-form connects to the next segment, continuing the explanation. This passage describes the cycle: Yu Yevon takes over the aeon → transforms it into Sin → is protected by Sin → continues summoning.

text: エボンジュは召喚を続けるんだ a エンに / かっ でも君たちが終わらせるから
translation: …Yu Yevon continues to summon, endlessly. / But because you will put an end to it…

vocabulary.meaning: to put an end to, to finish (causative)

grammar: The transcription includes audio artifacts (「a エンに」「かっ」are likely noise or garbled text). The core meaning is clear: エボンジュは召喚を続けるんだ (Yu Yevon continues to summon) followed by the hopeful contrast でも君たちが終わらせるから (but because you will end it…). んだ marks a personal explanation.

text: 永遠なんてない
translation: There is no eternity.
grammar: A reprise of the thematic line from earlier. なんて dismisses the concept of eternity as unreal. Without のにね this time, it's stated more flatly — almost as a decree. The repetition reinforces the game's central theme.

text: ああ エボンジュはシンの中にいるよ
translation: Right — Yu Yevon is inside Sin.
grammar: ああ here is an acknowledgment before confirming the key fact. よ marks new or assertive information being conveyed to the listener. The fayth confirms the tactical information: to fight Yu Yevon, the party must go inside Sin.

text: ねえ言うな 僕たちも協力するから / エボンジュと戦うときは 必ず召喚してほしい
translation: Hey, don't mention it — we'll help too. / When you fight Yu Yevon, please be sure to summon us.
grammar: 言うな is a plain prohibition (V stem + な). 協力するから — から gives a reason or assurance: 'because we'll cooperate.' 〜てほしい expresses a request/desire for the listener to perform an action: 'I want you to summon us.' 必ず adds absolute certainty.

text: 君たちの剣や魔法じゃ倒せないとも / 読んで、必ずだよ。
translation: Your swords and magic won't be able to defeat it either. / Got it? It has to be without fail.

vocabulary.meaning: either, also (adding to a previous point)
here likely 'call me / summon me' (read: 呼んで, to call)

grammar: 〜じゃ倒せない — casual じゃ (=では) with potential negative: 'can't be defeated with X.' とも adds 'either/also.' 読んで is likely 呼んで (call/summon me) — a transcription variant. 必ずだよ is an emphatic insistence: 必ず (without fail) + だ (copula) + よ (assertion). The fayth is insisting they must be summoned.

text: はい。 / それから、君。
translation: Yes. / And then, you.
grammar: はい is a polite affirmative. それから君 — the fayth pivots to address Tidus specifically. The sentence is left incomplete, dramatically trailing off before the fayth's revelation to Tidus about his nature. The pause created by the incomplete sentence builds anticipation.

text: すべてが終わったら、僕たちは夢見ることをやめる。
translation: When everything is over, we will stop dreaming.

vocabulary.meaning: when/if (conditional, marks completion of a condition)

grammar: 〜たら is a conditional meaning 'when/after X happens.' Here すべてが終わったら = 'when everything has ended.' 夢見ることをやめる uses the nominalizer こと to turn the verb 夢見る into a noun phrase ('the act of dreaming'), which becomes the object of やめる.

text: 僕たちの夢は、消える。
translation: Our dream will disappear.

vocabulary.meaning: to disappear, to vanish, to fade away

grammar: Simple declarative sentence with the subject marked by は. 消える (intransitive) means the dream vanishes on its own — no external agent causes it. The fayth are announcing that Tidus's existence as their dream will end.

text: うん。あんたたち、長い間頑張ったもんな。
translation: Yeah. You guys have worked hard for a long time, haven't you.

vocabulary.meaning: you guys, you all (informal plural second-person)
to do one's best, to hang in there, to work hard
you know (sentence-final, expressing empathy or acknowledgment)

grammar: 〜もんな (contracted from もの + な) is a casual sentence-final particle expressing soft acknowledgment or sympathetic agreement — roughly 'you have, haven't you.' Tidus says this with warmth toward the fayth who have been dreaming for centuries.

text: ごめん。 / お疲れさん。
translation: Sorry. / You've worked hard. (Thank you for your efforts.)

vocabulary.meaning: good work, thanks for your hard work (casual form of お疲れ様)

grammar: お疲れさん is a casual variant of お疲れ様でした, used to acknowledge someone's effort or signal that their work is done. The slash indicates two separate utterances, likely by different speakers — Tidus's apology followed by his acknowledgment.

text: 何の話?
translation: What are you talking about?
grammar: 何の話? literally 'talk of what?' — an informal question asking about the topic of conversation. の is the possessive/attributive particle connecting 何 to 話. The question mark and rising intonation imply genuine puzzlement.

text: 何でもない
translation: It's nothing.

vocabulary.meaning: it's nothing, never mind, it doesn't matter

grammar: 何でもない is a set expression: 何 (what) + でも (even/any) + ない (not) = 'nothing at all.' Used to deflect or dismiss a question. Tidus is hiding the truth about what the fayth's words mean for his own existence.

text: そんな顔すんなよ
translation: Don't make that face.

vocabulary.meaning: don't do (contracted colloquial prohibition: するな → すんな)

grammar: すんな is a colloquial contraction of するな (do not do). よ at the end softens and personalizes the command slightly. そんな顔 = 'that kind of face/expression.' Tidus notices someone looks worried and tells them not to.

text: 俺たちシンを倒せるんだぞ / もっと嬉しそうな顔しろよ
translation: We can defeat Sin, you know! / Show a happier face!

vocabulary.meaning: can defeat, able to beat (potential form of 倒す)
you know, I'm telling you (emphatic sentence-final)
to make a face, to wear an expression

grammar: 〜んだぞ is emphatic: んだ adds explanatory nuance ('the fact is…') and ぞ adds assertive masculine energy. もっと嬉しそうな顔しろよ: 〜そうな is an adjectival suffix meaning 'appearing/seeming ~'; しろよ is a mild command (imperative of する + よ).

text: 何か隠してるよね
translation: You're hiding something, aren't you.

vocabulary.meaning: is doing, ongoing state (contracted form of 〜ている)

grammar: 〜てる is a colloquial contraction of 〜ている indicating an ongoing state or action. よね combines よ (assertion) and ね (seeking agreement), forming a soft accusation that invites confirmation.

text: 隠してない
translation: I'm not hiding anything.

vocabulary.meaning: not doing (contracted negative of 〜ていない)

grammar: 隠してない is the colloquial contraction of 隠していない — the negative progressive/stative form. Tidus flatly denies the accusation, but the audience knows he is lying.

text: 本当に?
translation: Really?
grammar: A simple question formed by adding に (adverbial) to 本当 (truth/reality) and ending with rising intonation. Often contracted in speech to ほんとに?. Used here to press for confirmation with gentle skepticism.

text: 頼んでもいい? / ああ、そうそう!
translation: May I ask a favour? / Oh, right, right!

vocabulary.meaning: to ask, to request, to beg
it's okay to do ~, may I ~ (asking permission)
right right, exactly, that's it (recollection or agreement)

grammar: 頼んでもいい? is a permission request: 〜てもいい = 'is it okay if I~?' The て-form of 頼む + もいい. ああ、そうそう is an exclamation of sudden recollection.

text: えっとね、できるだけ大勢の人に伝えてほしいんだけど
translation: Um, I want you to tell as many people as possible, but…

vocabulary.meaning: large number of people, many people
to tell, to convey, to pass on

grammar: 〜てほしいんだけど uses ほしい to express a desire for another person's action. んだ adds explanatory weight; けど (but) at the end trails off, softening the request. できるだけ + noun phrase = 'as many ~ as possible.'

text: はい、なんでしょう?
translation: Yes, what is it?

vocabulary.meaning: what might it be? (polite, attentive inquiry)

grammar: なんでしょう is the polite volitional form of なんだ ('what is it?'). でしょう (from です) adds deference and openness. Used here as a polite prompt for the other person to continue.

text: 空を飛ぶ船が祈りの歌を歌う / それが聞こえたら、みんなも一緒に歌ってください
translation: A ship that flies through the sky will sing a song of prayer. / When you hear it, please everyone sing together.
grammar: 空を飛ぶ船 is a relative clause: 飛ぶ modifies 船 ('a ship that flies'). それが聞こえたら is another 〜たら conditional: 'when/if that is heard.' 歌ってください is a polite request: て-form + ください.

text: スピラジュに伝えてくれ / 意味がわかりません
translation: Tell all of Spira. / I don't understand what you mean.
grammar: 〜てくれ is a direct informal request (て-form + くれ). 意味がわかりません: が marks the subject of わかる ('understanding happens'), making this 'as for meaning, [it] doesn't occur to me' — a natural way to express not understanding.

text: なんでもいいの!このまま伝えて
translation: It doesn't matter! Just tell it exactly as it is!

vocabulary.meaning: anything is fine, it doesn't matter
just as it is, as-is, exactly like this

grammar: なんでもいい expresses that the exact content doesn't matter — literally 'anything is fine.' のは at the end of the first clause adds emphasis/explanation. このまま = 'in this state/form,' so このまま伝えて = 'just pass it on verbatim.' て-form alone (伝えて) is a casual request.

text: 空を飛ぶ船が祈りの歌を歌う。それが聞こえたら、みんなも一緒に歌ってください。ですね。
translation: A ship flying through the sky will sing a song of prayer. When you hear it, please everyone sing together. Is that right?
grammar: The messenger repeats back the message verbatim, then appends ですね as a confirmation tag ('That's what you said, right?'). This is a classic Japanese conversational strategy for confirming one has understood correctly.

text: それでシンを倒せるかもしれないんだ。 / 本当ですか?はい。すごいです。任せてください。スピラ中に伝えます。
translation: That might be how we can defeat Sin. / Really? Yes. That's amazing. Leave it to us. We'll spread the word throughout Spira.
grammar: かもしれないんだ: かもしれない (might be) + んだ (explanatory, assertive nuance). 任せてください is a request meaning 'please leave it to me/us.' 伝えます is a polite volitional/future form of 伝える.

text: いよいよってわけだな / シンの中にエボンジュってのがいるんだ
translation: So it's finally time. / There's something called Yu Yevon inside Sin.

vocabulary.meaning: finally, at last, now at last
so that means ~, so that's the situation (explanatory conclusion)

grammar: いよいよってわけだな: いよいよ (at last) + ってわけだ (that means / so it is) + な (softening/reflective). エボンジュってのがいる: ってのが is colloquial for というものが — 'something called Yu Yevon is (there).' A Wakka-style casual explanation.

text: そいつを倒す / ずいぶん単純な答えじゃねえか
translation: We defeat that thing. / That's a pretty simple answer, isn't it.

vocabulary.meaning: that guy, that thing (colloquial, slightly rough)
isn't it?, don't you think? (rough colloquial tag question)

grammar: じゃねえか is a colloquial (masculine/rough) contraction of じゃないか — a rhetorical tag question expressing mild surprise or irony. The first clause そいつを倒す is a bare dictionary-form verb used as a declaration of intent.

text: 複雑じゃなくてよかったろ / そりゃそうだ
translation: Good thing it's not complicated. / Well, that's true.

vocabulary.meaning: it's a good thing it wasn't ~
well of course, that's true (colloquial agreement)

grammar: 〜じゃなくてよかった: じゃない (not) + て-form + よかった (was good) = 'it's good that it wasn't ~.' ろ at the end is a casual sentence-final particle (≈ だろう) implying 'right?' or just softening. そりゃ is a contraction of それは.

text: あれ頼むよ
translation: I'm counting on that.

vocabulary.meaning: that (thing over there, refers to something known to both speakers)
to request, to rely on, I'm counting on you

grammar: 頼むよ used with a direct object (あれ) means 'I'm counting on that' or 'please take care of that.' よ adds a light emphasis. あれ refers to something visually salient — likely the airship or the plan just discussed.

text: あれだ
translation: That's it.
grammar: あれだ is a minimal declarative: 'That is it.' Used when pointing out something that both parties can see or recall. Context makes the referent clear without naming it.

text: あれだ
translation: That's it.
grammar: Repeated for emphasis or by a different speaker confirming the same observation. あれだ serves as a pointing declaration in context where the referent is visually or situationally apparent.

text: どうだ
translation: How about that? / Well?

vocabulary.meaning: how is it?, how about that? (seeking reaction or opinion)

grammar: どうだ is a very terse rhetorical or genuine question meaning 'How is it?' / 'What do you think?' Used after showing or doing something to prompt a reaction. The だ makes it direct and masculine in register.

text: バッチリ!
translation: Perfect! / Flawless!

vocabulary.meaning: perfect, flawless, spot-on (colloquial exclamation of approval)

grammar: バッチリ is an onomatopoeic/mimetic adverb used as a standalone exclamation meaning 'perfect!' or 'right on!' It can also be used predicatively (バッチリだ). Common in casual, energetic speech.

text: 空飛ぶ船が歌う…か…
translation: A sky-flying ship will sing… huh…

vocabulary.meaning: huh, I see, is that so (reflective sentence-final particle)

grammar: The repeated か at the end is a reflective/internal particle — not a real question, but a murmured 'is that so…' as the speaker processes something. The ellipses (…) indicate trailing-off, thoughtful hesitation. This is Tidus reflecting on the plan.

text: あとは、みんなが歌ってくれればいいんだけどな
translation: All that's left is to hope everyone sings for us.

vocabulary.meaning: as for the rest, all that remains
if (someone) does ~ for us (conditional of 〜てくれる)
it would be good if ~, all we need is ~
though, but (trailing expression of wish or mild uncertainty)

grammar: 〜てくれればいい: if someone does the favor (くれる = give/do for me), then it's good — expressing a wish or reliance. んだけどな at the end is a trailing qualifier expressing 'I hope so, but…' — a wistful tone.

text: シン!
translation: Sin!

vocabulary.meaning: Sin (the great monster that plagues Spira)

grammar: A single exclamatory noun, indicating that Sin has been sighted or is approaching. Exclamatory bare nouns are common in action contexts in Japanese.

text: よし!行くぞ! / どうやってシンの中に入るんだ?
translation: Alright! Let's go! / How do we get inside Sin?
grammar: よし is an exclamation of determination. ぞ is an assertive, typically masculine sentence-final particle. どうやって introduces a question about means/method. 〜んだ adds an explanatory or wondering nuance to the question — 'how is it that we get in?'

text: 一番単純な方法しかないっす! / だね!
translation: There's only the simplest method! / Right!

vocabulary.meaning: there is only ~, no option but ~ (restrictive)
polite sentence-final (contraction of です, casual-polite)

grammar: 〜しかない expresses exclusivity: 'there is nothing but X' / 'we have no choice but X.' っす is a youthful, casual-polite form of です. だね is a short agreement: 'that's right, yeah.'

text: じゃあ行きましょう
translation: Then let's go.

vocabulary.meaning: then, well then, in that case

grammar: じゃあ is a casual conjunction meaning 'well then' or 'in that case.' 行きましょう is the polite volitional form of 行く — an invitation or proposal to do something together.

text: おい何やらかすってんだよ
translation: Hey, what do you think you're doing?!

vocabulary.meaning: to do something reckless/outrageous, to pull off something crazy
what do you mean you're ~, what the heck are you doing (emphatic colloquial)

grammar: ってんだよ is a highly contracted and emphatic form: というんだよ → ってんだよ. It expresses exasperation or disbelief — 'just what are you saying you're doing?!' おい is a rough attention-grabbing interjection.

text: 口から入るか真の体に穴開けるかどっちかだな
translation: Either we go in through the mouth, or we blast a hole in Sin's body — one of the two.

vocabulary.meaning: one of the two, either one

grammar: 〜か〜かどっちかだな is a binary choice structure: 'either A or B, one of the two.' か after each option presents alternatives. だな at the end is a soft assertion seeking implicit agreement (masculine/casual).

text: そらまた どえらい作戦じゃねえか! / トウサギ!
translation: Now that's one hell of a plan! / Hey you!

vocabulary.meaning: outrageous, incredible, tremendous (intensified form of えらい)
isn't it!, what a ~ (rough rhetorical tag)

grammar: どえらい is an intensified colloquial adjective (ど is an intensifying prefix common in Kansai-influenced speech). じゃねえか here is exclamatory — 'isn't that something!' rather than a genuine question. Wakka's distinctive rough speech register.

text: おう! / あれだな! / あれか!
translation: Yeah! / That's it! / That one!

vocabulary.meaning: that's it, that's the one (pointing out with agreement)

grammar: Short exclamations. おう is a rough/masculine form of affirmation. な after だ seeks light confirmation. か turns あれだ into a question seeking confirmation — 'is that the one?'

text: おうよ! / 風をなけてやっからよ!
translation: You bet! / I'll give you a tailwind!

vocabulary.meaning: you bet!, that's right! (emphatic rough affirmative)
to do for (someone), to do (with a sense of doing a favor or assertive action)

grammar: おうよ is an emphatic affirmative (おう + よ). 風をなけてやっからよ appears to be colloquial/dialectal — likely 投げてやるから (I'll throw/send the wind at you) or 向けてやるから (I'll direct the wind at you). やる (do/give) + から (because/so) + よ (emphasis) = assertive promise.

text: そっから飛び込め! / うっす! / 気をつけろなんて言わねえ
translation: Dive in from there! / Yes sir! / I won't tell you to be careful.

vocabulary.meaning: from there (contraction of そこから)
yes sir! (contracted emphatic はい/押忍, used in sports/martial contexts)
to be careful, to take care

grammar: 飛び込め is the imperative of 飛び込む — a direct command. うっす is an energetic subordinate's acknowledgment. 気をつけろなんて言わねえ: なんて + verb means 'something like ~'; ねえ is rough negative of ない. The whole phrase expresses gruff encouragement — 'I'm not going to coddle you with be careful.'

text: もう一切りやってこい! / うっす!
translation: Go and finish this! / Yes sir!

vocabulary.meaning: one round, one stretch, one go
to go and do, to go take care of
go and do ~ and come back (imperative of 〜てくる)

grammar: 〜てこい is the imperative of 〜てくる (go and do something and return). It implies 'go take care of this and come back.' The combination with もう一切り = 'go do this one thing' — a send-off command.

text: よせ!
translation: Stop! / Don't!

vocabulary.meaning: stop it!, don't! (imperative of よす, meaning to cease)

grammar: よせ is the imperative form of よす (to stop, to cease). It is blunt and urgent — a one-word command to stop an action immediately. Common in tense action scenes.

text: リュック! / た…の…む…
translation: Rikku! / I… beg… you…
grammar: た…の…む… is 頼む broken apart by ellipses, indicating extreme effort or pain — the speaker can barely get the word out. This is a plea for help. Calling someone's name before making a desperate request is a deeply emotional Japanese speech pattern.

text: まかせとけ!
translation: Leave it to me!

vocabulary.meaning: leave it to me! (contracted imperative: 任せておけ → まかせとけ)

grammar: まかせとけ is a contracted form of 任せておけ — the imperative of 任せておく (to leave something in someone's care). It's a confident, energetic assurance: 'you can count on me, just leave it!'

text: 聞こえるよ
translation: I can hear it.

vocabulary.meaning: to be audible, to hear (spontaneous perception)

grammar: 聞こえる is the spontaneous/potential verb 'to be heard' — Japanese distinguishes between 聞く (intentionally listen) and 聞こえる (sounds reach the ears). よ is a mild assertive particle here. The people of Spira can hear the Hymn of the Fayth being sung.

text: 本当だわ
translation: It's true.
grammar: だわ is a sentence-final particle combination associated with feminine speech — softly assertive. 本当だわ = 'it really is true' or 'so it is.' Expresses gentle surprise or confirmation.

text: みんな歌ってくれてる!
translation: Everyone is singing for us!

vocabulary.meaning: to do (something) for the speaker's benefit

grammar: くれてる is a contraction of くれている — the progressive form of 〜てくれる. This verb expresses that the action is done for the speaker's benefit. みんなが歌ってくれている = 'everyone is singing for us.' The emotional payoff of the plan working.

text: 期待に応えるっす!
translation: I'll live up to their expectations!

vocabulary.meaning: polite assertion (casual-polite contraction of です)

grammar: 期待に応える is a set phrase: 'to meet/live up to expectations.' に marks the target/direction (expectations). っす is a youthful, casual-polite sentence-final (contraction of です). The speaker is energetically committing to not let people down.

text: 言うな!
translation: Don't say it!
grammar: Plain form verb + な is a direct negative imperative: 'don't do X.' This is blunt and urgent. Someone is cutting off what another person is about to say — perhaps to prevent a jinx or an emotional moment.

text: これ、もういらないだろ? / ああ! / あ、い、いったな…
translation: This — we don't need it anymore, right? / Yeah! / Ah, he… he threw it…
grammar: いらないだろ? is a tag question seeking agreement: 'we don't need this anymore, right?' だろ is a casual contraction of だろう. あ、い、いったな — the broken speech (い, い…) indicates surprise or emotion. いった (went/did) followed by な (reflective) = 'oh, he went and did it…'

text: いらないよな!
translation: We don't need it, right!
grammar: よな is a combination of よ (assertion) and な (seeking agreement) — making a confident statement that also checks for agreement. More assertive than ね alone. This line echoes the previous, amplifying the moment of discarding something (likely Tidus's father's sphere).

text: うん!
translation: Yeah!
grammar: うん is the casual, informal equivalent of はい. Short and direct, expressing agreement or simple confirmation.

text: おいおいおいおい! / なんか、やばいぞ!
translation: Hey hey hey hey! / Something's bad — this is dangerous!

vocabulary.meaning: hey hey, come on (repeated interjection of alarm or exasperation)
dangerous, bad, in trouble (slang; originally means 'risky/sketchy')

grammar: おいおい repeated four times conveys escalating alarm. やばいぞ: やばい is a colloquial adjective meaning something is dangerously bad or off. ぞ adds urgent, masculine emphasis. なんか softens/vaguens the statement ('something' rather than something specific).

text: くそ親父!
translation: Damn old man! / You bastard, Dad!

vocabulary.meaning: old man, dad (informal, can be affectionate or rough)

grammar: くそ is used as an intensifying prefix or expletive (like 'damn'). くそ親父 = 'damn old man' or 'that bastard father' — rough and emotional. This is Tidus confronting Jecht who has become the Final Aeon. The word choice shows both anger and the intimacy of a son.

text: おい! 真の腕のところを光ったの見えたか?
translation: Hey! Did you see that glowing spot on Sin's arm?

vocabulary.meaning: to shine, to glow, to light up
to be visible, to be seen

grammar: 光ったの: の here is a nominalizer turning 光った (glowed/lit up) into a noun phrase ('the thing that glowed'). 見えたか? is a past-tense question using the spontaneous verb 見える (to be visible) — 'did you see/could you see?' 真の腕 refers to Sin's arm.

text: あれは絶対なんかあるぜ! / やるに!ごっきさ!
translation: There's definitely something there! / Let's do it! Go for it!
grammar: 絶対なんかあるぜ: 絶対 strengthens the assertion ('there must absolutely be something'). なんか is colloquial for なにか. ぜ is a rough, masculine emphatic particle. The second part appears to be battle chatter/dialect — excited and energetic speech.

text: シンシ! 道も変なえせんが!
translation: Sin! The path's also going strange!
grammar: This segment contains heavily distorted audio transcription. The underlying meaning appears to be a warning that the path or navigation is becoming erratic as they approach or fight Sin. も indicates 'also' — adding to previous concerns.

text: シンに引き寄せられてるって!
translation: We're being drawn in by Sin!

vocabulary.meaning: to draw toward, to pull close
I'm telling you!, I said ~ (emphatic quotation particle)

grammar: 引き寄せられてる is the passive progressive of 引き寄せる: 'is being drawn toward.' シンに = by Sin (に marks the agent in passive constructions). って at the end is emphatic — 'I'm telling you!' — adding urgency.

text: お前ら! 中に戻れ!
translation: You lot! Get back inside!
grammar: お前ら is a commanding plural second person — rough and authoritative. 戻れ is the imperative of 戻る. The combination is an urgent military-style command: 'Everyone get back inside (the ship)!'

text: オッサン! 近づいてくれ! / ガーッ! 少し待ってろ!
translation: Old man! Get closer! / Ugh! Wait a moment!

vocabulary.meaning: wait! (imperative of 待っている — stay and wait)

grammar: 〜てくれ is a direct informal request using the giving verb くれる. 待ってろ is an imperative of 待っている (be waiting) — 'keep waiting / stay there and wait.' ガーッ is a frustrated or strained exclamation.

text: 試しに一発かましてやら! / おいら!そこで待機しろ!
translation: Let me try hitting it once! / You lot! Stay on standby over there!

vocabulary.meaning: as a test, by way of trying
to land a hit, to give someone a blow (colloquial)

grammar: 試しに sets up the action as experimental ('as a trial'). かましてやら is colloquial for かましてやろう — the volitional 'I'll do it' (やる = do/give). 待機しろ is a military-style command: 'maintain standby position.'

text: 行くぞ!
translation: Here we go!
grammar: 行くぞ is a classic battle cry — 'We're going!' / 'Let's do this!' ぞ makes it forceful and masculine. The simple present tense here acts as an immediate declaration of action.

text: やった! / お前らもよくやったじゃねえか!
translation: We did it! / You guys did well too, didn't you!

vocabulary.meaning: we did it!, yes! (exclamation of success)
isn't it?, didn't you (rough rhetorical tag)

grammar: やった is the past tense of やる used as a celebratory exclamation — 'We did it!' よくやった: よく (well) + やった (did) = 'you did well.' じゃねえか makes it a rhetorical exclamation of praise rather than a genuine question.

text: よし!この勢いで、ハンダイガーもうやっちゅうぞ!
translation: Alright! With this momentum, let's take out the next one too!

vocabulary.meaning: with, by means of (particle indicating means)
let's do it!, gonna take care of (colloquial contraction of やってしまおう or やっちゃおう)

grammar: この勢いで = 'using/riding this momentum.' で marks the means/method. やっちゅうぞ is a strong colloquial contraction — likely やってしまおうぞ (let's go ahead and finish it off!) compressed into energetic dialect. ぞ adds emphatic masculine force.

text: 勝手に決めるな!
translation: Don't decide things on your own!

vocabulary.meaning: on one's own, without permission, selfishly

grammar: 決めるな is a blunt negative imperative (verb dictionary form + な), used among close friends or when angry. It is more forceful than 決めないでください.

text: おーしゃ!次はどこだよ!
translation: Alright! Where's next?!

vocabulary.meaning: alright! yeah! (casual exclamation of enthusiasm, variant of よし)
casual sentence ending asserting or asking something

grammar: 次はどこだよ uses the particle は to mark 次 as the topic. The sentence-final だよ adds a casual, energetic nuance. The question is formed without か — just rising intonation in speech.

text: トカニが… / ワロスはへぇ! / ヨエアな画面でよ!
translation: [Distorted/garbled battle chatter] Something's happening…! / Over there! / On that screen!
grammar: This segment contains heavily distorted or phonetically garbled speech — typical of chaotic battle scenes. The words トカニ and ワロス are likely corrupted versions of other words or Al Bhed speech. Only 画面 (screen) is clearly standard Japanese.

text: シュホン、壊れたってさ…
translation: The [cannon/weapon], apparently it's broken…

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final particle adding a casual, matter-of-fact tone

grammar: 壊れたってさ uses the quotative って to relay information heard from someone else (hearsay). The trailing さ softens the delivery while the pause (…) conveys resignation.

text: 仕方ねえ! / お前ら戻れ! / 作戦ねりがおーし!
translation: Can't be helped! / Everyone fall back! / Let's regroup and come up with a plan!

vocabulary.meaning: can't be helped, no choice (colloquial: 仕方ねえ)
you guys, you lot (rough, masculine plural)
to work out, to refine (a plan)

grammar: 戻れ is a direct imperative (verb stem + れ for Group 1 verbs). 仕方ねえ is the rough masculine contraction of 仕方ない. 作戦ねりがおーし is casual battle speech meaning 'let's work out a strategy.'

text: いいや、行くっす! / 勢いがある時は、勢いに乗るっす!
translation: No way, we're going! / When you've got momentum, you ride it!

vocabulary.meaning: to ride, to go with, to take advantage of
casual polite ending (contracted form of です, used by younger speakers)

grammar: 勢いに乗る is a set phrase meaning 'to ride the momentum.' The っす ending is Tidus's signature speech style — informal yet with a veneer of politeness.

text: これ、ブリッツの鉄則!
translation: That's the iron rule of blitzball!

vocabulary.meaning: iron rule, cardinal rule, inviolable principle

grammar: This is a nominal sentence (no verb): これ [は] ブリッツの鉄則 [だ] — topic and copula are both dropped for punchy effect. 鉄則 literally means 'iron rule' and carries a sense of unbreakable law.

text: あんたといると退屈しないわ
translation: I never get bored when I'm with you.

vocabulary.meaning: when one is with ~, being with ~
to be bored, to feel bored
sentence-final particle (feminine softening or mild emphasis)

grammar: 〜といると is a conditional/circumstantial structure (と + いる + と) meaning 'when/while being with ~.' The negative しない + わ creates a gentle, wry affirmation — Lulu's characteristic dry humor.

text: 待てよ!エースは俺だっつーの!
translation: Hold on! I'm the ace here!

vocabulary.meaning: hold on, wait a minute (casual imperative)
I'm telling you it's ~! (emphatic colloquial assertion, from だって言うの)

grammar: だっつーの is a very casual contraction of だって言うの, used to insist on something emphatically. The whole phrase エースは俺だっつーの expresses Tidus's competitive frustration.

text: とえ、とえ、きゅ、何えメネも!! / それでも連鎖やガノフだ!
translation: [Garbled battle shouting] / Even so, keep the chain going!
grammar: The first part of this segment is heavily distorted battle noise. それでも functions as a concessive conjunction ('even so/despite that'), pivoting to a command to maintain the attack chain.

text: 金義メネべ御不存しんげ!! / リュック!
translation: [Garbled/distorted exclamation] / Rikku!
grammar: The first phrase appears to be heavily corrupted speech, possibly Al Bhed mixed with distorted Japanese during an intense battle sequence. Only リュック is clearly intelligible — someone calling out to Rikku.

text: 達せほ!
translation: [Battle cry / garbled exclamation]
grammar: This is a distorted or phonetically garbled exclamation from a chaotic battle scene. It does not correspond to standard Japanese vocabulary and is likely a transcription artifact or in-universe distorted speech.

text: 復活…するかな?
translation: Will it… revive, I wonder?

vocabulary.meaning: to do, to happen (here: to revive)

grammar: かな at the end of a sentence expresses gentle self-directed wondering. The pause (…) before するかな heightens the anxiety. The subject is omitted — understood from context to be Sin.

text: たぶんな
translation: Probably.

vocabulary.meaning: sentence-final particle expressing mild reflection or resignation (masculine)

grammar: A minimalist two-word response. たぶんな acknowledges a grim probability without elaborating — the な adds a resigned, quiet masculine tone, implying 'yeah, probably so.'

text: なんで!?そうなのかよ!
translation: Why?! So that's how it is?!

vocabulary.meaning: is that so?, so that's the case?

grammar: そうなのか is formed from そう (so/that way) + な (copula in plain form) + のか (seeking confirmation/explanation). The よ adds emotional force. The overall tone is surprise and frustration.

text: シンの中にいる奴を倒さなくちゃならない / これだけで倒せたら、飛ばす隊だって苦労しねえよな
translation: We have to defeat the one inside Sin. / If we could beat it with just this, even the Crusaders wouldn't have had to struggle.

vocabulary.meaning: guy, one, the thing/person (casual, slightly rough)
to struggle, to have a hard time

grammar: なくちゃならない is a colloquial contraction of なければならない (must/have to). これだけで means 'with just this alone.' 〜だって苦労しねえ = 'even ~ wouldn't have struggled' — a counterfactual.

text: でも、シンを弱らせたのは確かじゃない?
translation: But we definitely weakened Sin, didn't we?

vocabulary.meaning: to weaken, to make weaker (causative of 弱る)

grammar: 弱らせた is the causative past form of 弱る (to weaken) — 'we caused it to weaken.' のは nominalization. 確かじゃない is a tag question seeking agreement, typical of Rikku's upbeat framing of grim situations.

text: そうだよ、そうだよ! / よし、今のうちに手法の修理だい
translation: Right, right! / Okay, let's repair the weapons while we have the chance!

vocabulary.meaning: while we have the chance, while we still can

grammar: 今のうちに is a useful set phrase meaning 'while there's still opportunity/time.' It implies urgency — do it before the window closes. 〜だい at the end is a casual declarative exclamation.

text: ジェクトさん 苦しいのかな?
translation: I wonder if Jecht is in pain.

vocabulary.meaning: I wonder if ~, is it that ~? (soft introspective question)

grammar: のかな combines the nominalizing の (which turns the preceding clause into a noun-like question) with かな (wondering). The result is a gentle, inward-directed question — Tidus quietly wondering about his father trapped inside Sin.

text: 終わらせよ 早く 祈り後も協力してくれるっていうしさ / あの言い方 気になるんだ
translation: Let's end this quickly. The fayth said they'd help too. / That way they said it… it bothers me.

vocabulary.meaning: to end, to finish, to bring to an end (causative)
to bother one, to be on one's mind, to worry about

grammar: 終わらせよ is a volitional-imperative form (softer than a direct command) — 'let's end it.' 〜っていうし means 'they said ~ and so' (quoting a reason). 気になるんだ uses んだ to express that something is genuinely on his mind.

text: ずっと一緒に戦ってくれてたのに 今になって協力するなんて
translation: They've been fighting together with us all along, and yet now they say they'll 'cooperate'…

vocabulary.meaning: all along, the whole time, continuously
to do something for one's benefit
even though ~, despite the fact that ~ (expresses contrast or mild reproach)
only now, at this late stage

grammar: 〜のに here expresses a contradictory or unexpected situation — 'despite having done X, now Y.' 今になって emphasizes the lateness or oddness of the timing, suggesting something feels off about the fayth's wording.

text: まあ ない
translation: Well… nothing [we can do].
grammar: A very compressed expression. まあ ない implies 仕方がない ('there's nothing to be done') — the subject and predicate are almost entirely dropped. It is a resigned acknowledgment that, whatever the fayth meant, the party has no choice but to press on.

text: シンが復活するのは、エボンジュが召喚獣に乗り移るから…だよね。
translation: Sin revives because Yu Yevon possesses the aeon… right?

vocabulary.meaning: to transfer into, to possess (a body)
right?, isn't that so? (seeking gentle confirmation)

grammar: This sentence uses のは…から construction to state a cause-effect relationship: 'the reason Sin revives (のは) is because (から) Yu Yevon possesses the aeon.' だよね softens it into a confirmatory question — Yuna is thinking aloud and seeking agreement.

text: 私が召喚したら、きっとエボンジュは乗り移ってくる。 / それは、小さなシン…だよね。
translation: If I summon an aeon, Yu Yevon will surely possess it. / That would be… a small Sin, right?
grammar: 〜たら is a conditional ('if/when I summon'). 乗り移ってくる uses the て-form + くる to indicate movement toward the speaker — 'will come and possess it.' The second sentence is Yuna's key insight: a possessed aeon = a miniature Sin they can actually fight.

text: ああ!
translation: Oh! [Realization]

vocabulary.meaning: ah!, oh! (exclamation of sudden understanding or realization)

grammar: ああ here is an interjection expressing sudden insight or recognition — someone has just understood what Yuna is proposing. Short, punchy, and emotionally loaded.

text: それなら、究極召喚じゃなくても倒せるかも!
translation: If that's the case, we might be able to defeat it without the Final Summoning!

vocabulary.meaning: if that's the case, in that case

vocabulary.reading: きゅうきょくしょうかん

vocabulary.meaning: might ~, maybe ~ (shortened かもしれない)

grammar: それなら is a conditional pivot — 'given that, then.' 〜じゃなくても means 'even without' — so 究極召喚じゃなくても倒せる means 'can defeat it even without the Final Summoning.' かも (short for かもしれない) adds hopeful uncertainty.

text: 倒しても、またエボンジュが乗り移るよ。
translation: Even if we defeat it, Yu Yevon will just possess another one.
grammar: 〜ても is a concessive conditional — 'even if we defeat it.' The implication is that defeating the aeon alone is insufficient because Yu Yevon will simply move to the next one. This is the fayth's sobering clarification.

text: そうなったらまた倒す!
translation: Then when that happens, we defeat it again!

vocabulary.meaning: if/when that happens, in that case

grammar: そうなったら is a conditional using the past form of なる (to become) + たら — 'if/when it comes to that.' The simple, defiant 倒す at the end (dictionary form used as a declaration) captures Tidus's stubborn, forward-charging personality.

text: 最後にはエボンジュは 駅場をなくしてさ!
translation: In the end, Yu Yevon will run out of places to go!

vocabulary.meaning: in the end, ultimately, at last
to lose, to run out of

grammar: 最後には introduces the ultimate conclusion. 駅場をなくして likely refers to running out of hosts/vessels (the phrasing is colloquial/slightly garbled but the meaning is clear in context). The さ ending is casual and confident.

text: やらなくちゃ… / ならないんだよね?
translation: We have to do it… / That's what it comes down to, right?

vocabulary.meaning: have to ~, must ~ (contraction of なければ)
